Record Class GTNetProtocolDescriptor

java.lang.Object
java.lang.Record
grafiosch.gtnet.GTNetProtocolDescriptor
Record Components:
code - the message code this describes
category - request, response or announcement — this decides the send path and the handler contract
userInitiable - an administrator may submit this code from the message dialog
requiresResponse - the request stays open until one of validResponses() arrives; such a request is delete-protected and blocks the deletion of its peer
validResponses - the codes that legitimately answer this one; empty for everything but a request and the threadable admin message
model - the payload model class, null when the code carries no parameters
formEligible - the model fields are filled in by the user, so the code belongs in /msgformdefinition. False for a payload the server builds itself, such as the handshake token
repeatSendAsMany - how often a delivery of this code may be attempted
reprocessable - a repeated delivery may simply be processed again instead of being answered from the stored outcome — true only for a query that mutates nothing
inboundDispatch - the code can arrive as an inbound message of its own and therefore needs a handler. False for an answer that is only ever read out of the synchronous reply envelope
threadable - the code may carry a replyTo without being a registered response of anything; this is what lets two administrators hold a conversation in admin messages
autoAnswerRequest - the code may be the requestMsgCode of a GTNetMessageAnswer rule
autoAnswerResponse - the code may be the responseMsgCode of a rule. False for a refusal the server issues on its own, which an administrator must not be able to configure as an answer
senderPersists - the sender writes a gt_net_message row before it sends, so its envelope can name that row in idSourceGtNetMessage. False for a machine-to-machine code whose sender keeps no row at all — the ping and the payload exchanges — whose envelope therefore carries no sender-local id and whose delivery is outside the idempotency mechanism
public record GTNetProtocolDescriptor(GTNetMessageCode code, MessageCategory category, boolean userInitiable, boolean requiresResponse, List<GTNetMessageCode> validResponses, Class<?> model, boolean formEligible, byte repeatSendAsMany, boolean reprocessable, boolean inboundDispatch, boolean threadable, boolean autoAnswerRequest, boolean autoAnswerResponse, boolean senderPersists) extends Record
Everything the system knows about one GTNet message code.

The protocol used to be described by six overlapping registries — a code registry, a response map on the application enum, a model map, two frontend constants and a hardcoded list of "codes that await a reply" — none of them complete and no two of them in agreement. A descriptor is the single statement about a code: which category it belongs to, whether a person may send it, which codes answer it, what payload it carries, whether it needs a handler and whether it may appear in an auto-answer rule.

Nothing is derived from the name of the code. The naming convention lies often enough to be unusable: GT_NET_FIRST_HANDSHAKE_SEL_RR_S is user-initiated yet ends in _S, and the _RR_ marker is absent from codes that do wait for an answer. Where a fact matters, it is declared.

    • blocksDeletion

      public boolean blocksDeletion()
      Whether a still unanswered instance of this code prevents the deletion of the message and of the peer it belongs to. A request whose answer is outstanding must not be removable, or the conversation loses the row the answer would attach to.
      Returns:
      true when a pending instance is delete-protected
